You will be managing a team of engineers who individually possess experience in:

On-Premise Linux systems, Container solutions, Debian packaging, Ansible, data streaming and queuing technologies such as Kafka or RabbitMQ
Advanced database management knowledge (MySQL, Postgres) in replicated environments.
Physical Network management, with an on-prem estate that is Juniper focused. 
Cloud environments: GCP and AWS
Platform engineer focused on building, maintaining and supporting an Internal Developer Platform (CI/CD)

 
The Operational Reality
It is important to be transparent about the environment you are joining. We operate at high velocity with a broad and complex technology estate. However, we are a lean team, not a giant corporation with endless resources.

Context Switching is the Norm

You will rarely have the luxury of focusing on a single task for weeks at a time. You will be required to shift focus multiple times a week, and sometimes multiple times a day, as business priorities evolve.

Agility over Silos

Because we are a lean team, we wear many hats. You must be comfortable pivoting from a strategic discussion to an operational challenge without losing momentum.

Significant experience leading a technical team, with a specific focus on the people management aspect (performance reviews, career growth etc).

Deep knowledge of and experience with ITIL practices, with the ability to apply them to improve team workflows. Demonstrated ability to apply Lean Six Sigma concepts.

title: Platform Security Engineer
description_clean:
At Scality, we build software that stores and protects the world’s most critical data — running on Linux, inside some of the largest infrastructures on the planet, at exabyte scale, for organizations that cannot afford to fail.
We are looking for a Platform Security Engineer to join our platform and delivery team in Paris. This is a new seat, and it exists because security work needs dedicated capacity. Absorbed as background tasks between feature tickets, it never gets the focus it deserves. You would be that dedicated capacity.
This is a Linux-first, hands-on engineering role. You will not write policies for other people to implement — you will write the Python and Bash that hardens our OS, automates our vulnerability management, and proves to auditors and customers that our supply chain is sound.

About ScalityScality is the leader in software-defined object storage, trusted by 1,000+ enterprises and 700M+ users worldwide across banking, healthcare, and government sectors — exactly the sectors where security posture is a purchasing criterion, not a checkbox.
Industry recognition:

Gartner Magic Quadrant Leader for 9 consecutive years — the only 100% software-defined storage company to hold this position since the quadrant’s inception
#1 on the GigaOm Radar for Enterprise Object Storage (2024), ahead of 17 competing vendors
Gold Stevie Award 2025 — ARTESCA 3.0, Cloud Storage & Backup Solution category
Net Promoter Score of 85 across RING and ARTESCA
About the team
You will join a small team of highly skilled Linux engineers responsible for delivering and maintaining ADI (Scality Autonomous Data Infrastructure), our full platform: RING (object storage), S3C (S3-compatible layer), and SCOS (Scality OS — our own Linux distribution).
The team works across the full stack of infrastructure engineering — deep Linux system integration, RPM packaging, CI/CD pipelines, monitoring, and release automation. The command line is where most of our day happens, and we ship a Linux distribution to customers.
How We Build
We build with AI tools, in earnest rather than as an experiment. Every engineer here has Claude Code, and it is part of how we write, review, and ship code day to day.
We are also designing something larger: an AI code and delivery factory — AI woven into the build and release chain itself, not just into the editor. That work is early and still being thought through rather than already solved. We expect it to become part of how we maintain the platform, and CVE remediation is one of the first places we think it fits: an automated path from advisory to assessment to a patched, tested, delivered build.
If that sounds like a problem you would want to work on, this role sits close to it.
One principle is not negotiable: a human owns the outcome. AI writes code here, and when it does, we own what it produces — the review, the decision to ship, the consequences, and the fix. “The tool did it” is not an explanation we accept from ourselves, and it is not one we would offer a customer. In security work that matters doubly: an answer you cannot defend is worse than no answer at all.
How This Role Works
Scality is building a network of security engineers across the engineering department — a security peer embedded in each development team, rather than a central security function working at arm’s length from the code. You would be that peer for the platform and delivery team.

Security priorities are owned by our VP of Engineering. The agenda is set at that level, with dedicated resources committed across the teams. You will not have to invent it alone — and you will have a voice in it: the engineers closest to the code help decide what goes on the roadmap. We will be straight with you: today security work competes with delivery commitments and too often loses. Naming an owner and funding dedicated people is how we intend to change that. You would help build that capability, not inherit a finished one.
The team is accountable for the deliveries. Security items sit on the team’s plate alongside everything else it commits to, rather than in a separate function filing tickets from the outside.
You are the dedicated resource that makes them happen. While your teammates carry releases, OS compatibility, and platform features, your time is reserved for the security work. That focus is the whole reason the seat exists.
You share the team’s perimeter and its knowledge. Same repositories, same Jira projects, same code reviews, same sprint rituals. The engineers around you have rare, hard-earned Linux depth — OS integration, RPM packaging, boot and GRUB, CI/CD, monitoring — and you will learn the platform from them.
You will have peers. Security engineers embedded in the other development teams work the same problems on different perimeters. That network is where you compare notes, share tooling, and grow into the craft.

The point of the model is that security decisions get made inside the team that builds and ships the product, by someone who understands the build system rather than filing tickets against it.
Your First Missions
Two priorities are already on the roadmap, and they will shape your first year.
1. CVE exposure, answered before it is asked
Customers in banking, healthcare, and government ask us, routinely and under their own audit obligations, whether our products are exposed to a given CVE. That will not stop — for them, asking is the compliance requirement. Today each answer is researched from scratch: a customer question becomes a ticket, the ticket becomes a hunt through SBOMs, vendor advisories, and our own configuration, and the round trip can take weeks to produce something the team is not fully confident defending.
Your first mission is to invert that, so the answer already exists when the question arrives.

A standing exposure record, per shipped component and per release: what the SBOM says is present, what the upstream vendor has decided (including “will not fix”, which is common on RHEL 8 and often the real answer), and whether the vulnerable code path is actually reachable in our configuration
Reachability over presence. A module shipped and loaded by a distribution default is not the same as a module configured on a live URL. That distinction is the difference between “vulnerable” and “no impact”, and it is where the engineering judgement lives
Continuous CVE detection across our repositories, vendored third-party modules, container images, and shipped RPMs
Wiring detection into our existing SBOM tooling and GitHub Actions pipelines, so exposure is computed when a release is built rather than when a customer asks
A defined interface with the security engineers and the customer-facing teams: who produces the technical assessment, who owns the wording that reaches the customer, and how both meet the response commitments in our customer security policy
Durable capture. An assessment that lives only in a ticket comment gets re-derived next release. Findings belong somewhere queryable
A remediation loop with clear ownership and response targets, integrated with how the team already works in Jira
AI-assisted remediation, where it fits: from advisory to proposed patch to a tested build, with a human deciding what ships

Done well, a customer’s “are you affected by X?” becomes a lookup and an afternoon, not an escalation and three weeks.
2. Raising the security baseline of SCOS
SCOS is our own Linux distribution — we control the kickstarts, the package set, the boot path, and the images. That is unusual leverage, and we intend to use it. You will drive platform-level hardening across the OS we ship:

A hardened, defensible default configuration for the distribution
Advancing SELinux enforcement across RING and S3C (work already begun on the team, which you will help carry)
Supply-chain integrity: artifact provenance, signing, dependency currency, reproducible and verifiable builds
Secrets and credential handling across the delivery pipeline
Cryptographic posture — including FIPS 140-3 readiness, which matters concretely: FIPS 140-2 certificates move to NIST’s historical list on 22 September 2026, and RHEL 9’s validated OpenSSL, GnuTLS, and kernel crypto modules are the foundation we build on
Compliance-driven engineering work, notably the supply-chain security expectations of NIS2 (Article 21(2)(d)) and the EU Cyber Resilience Act — translated into automation and evidence, not spreadsheets

You will also contribute to what comes next: threat modelling of the platform, hardening guidance for customers, and security review of significant design changes.
What We Are Looking For
This is a role for someone early in their career who wants to grow into being their team’s security reference. We expect to invest in you, and we expect you to keep growing here for as long as you want to — there is no ceiling built into this seat.
Required

Linux is your primary operating system — at work, at home, or both. You are comfortable in the terminal and you reach for a shell before a UI
Roughly 2–4 years of relevant experience, or a shorter track record with unusually strong evidence of the skills below
Solid working ability in Python and Bash — you will be writing and maintaining real code in a production codebase
A genuine, demonstrable interest in security. We care much more about this than about formal credentials. Show it however it is true for you: CTFs, a home lab, reading advisories and CVE writeups for fun, a hardening project, security-adjacent contributions, a blog, anything real
Comfortable using Git in a collaborative environment
Ability to read and understand existing code before modifying it
The judgement to tell a real risk from a scanner’s opinion — and the instinct to check whether vulnerable code is actually reachable before calling it exposed
The willingness to say plainly when you are not yet sure, rather than producing an answer you could not defend
French — the team works in French day to day
Written communication skills in English

Nice to Have

Powered by physics-based modeling, statistical mechanics, and generative AI, QEMI allows our teams to design novel drug candidates from first principles.
 
What makes AQEMIA different is our commitment to true innovation: our research is dedicated to the invention of new molecular entities, not the refinement of existing ones. We focus on inventing never-before-seen molecules, without relying on experimental data, and advancing them into a growing pipeline of proprietary programs and strategic partnerships with leading pharmaceutical companies.

AQEMIA brings together a diverse, multidisciplinary team of 80+ professionals based in Paris and London. Our scientists and engineers, including chemists, physicists, machine learning experts, and software engineers, work side by side to push the boundaries of early-stage drug discovery.

At AQEMIA, team members are encouraged to contribute their expertise, learn from one another, and play an active role in shaping the future of drug invention.

AQEMIA's drug discovery programs and AI platform increasingly create value through licensing deals and strategic partnerships with pharma and biotech companies.

title: AI Harness Engineer - Agentic & Autonomous Operations (m/f/x)
description_clean:
xHeron is building the Service-as-Software company for short-term rental operators. We take responsibility for guest communication, team coordination and issue resolution, so customers can hand over the work without handing over their business.
Today, we deliver that service through people, software and AI. We’re turning the expertise behind it into autonomous systems that understand situations, take action and follow through. Not another tool to supervise. A service that gets the job done.
We’re looking for an AI Engineer to build the agentic capabilities at the heart of xHeron. You’ll help shape how our agents reason, act and learn, and build a company where AI doesn’t just support the work, but increasingly delivers it.
Tasks
We are looking for an AI Harness Engineer to build the software layer that turns language models into dependable operational systems.
You will work on orchestration, context assembly, tool execution, state, permissions, evaluations, observability, failure recovery, and human handoffs. The goal is not merely to generate a good response.
What You’ll Own

Agent harness architecture: Build the control layer around models: task decomposition, state management, model and tool selection, execution loops, checkpoints, retries, stopping conditions, and human handoffs.
Decision and execution behavior: Design how agents interpret situations, choose actions, manage uncertainty, and complete bounded operational tasks—not only how they generate text.
Context and memory: Determine what an agent needs to know at each step. Build context assembly, retrieval, memory, evidence selection, and knowledge-maintenance strategies while managing relevance, latency, and cost.
Tools and real-world effects: Connect agents to APIs and operational systems through explicit tool contracts, permissions, validation, idempotency, and confirmation that the intended effect actually occurred.
Evaluation and regression testing: Build representative evaluation suites and automated tests for decision quality, tool use, task completion, safety, escalation behavior, and recurring failure patterns.
Observability and failure analysis: Make agent behavior inspectable through structured traces, state, outcomes, and error classification. Diagnose failures across models, prompts, context, tools, and surrounding software.
Continuous improvement: Use evaluations, production traces, operator feedback, and controlled experiments to improve prompts, context, tools, model choices, and agent architecture.
Production ownership: Ship and operate production Python software alongside our CTO and engineering team. Work closely with systems engineering on integrations, authorization, durable state, recovery, and safe execution.

Requirements
What Makes You a Great Fit

You are a strong software engineer who can design, build, test, and operate reliable production systems in Python.
You have built a substantial LLM-powered, automation, workflow, or decision system: not only notebooks, chat interfaces, prompt experiments, or a basic retrieval pipeline.
You understand the engineering layer around a model: orchestration, state, context, tools, structured outputs, permissions, retries, fallbacks, observability, and evaluations.
You can connect intelligence to real work: selecting relevant evidence, making a bounded decision, invoking tools or APIs, and verifying that the intended result occurred.
You design for partial failure and uncertainty. You think deliberately about when an agent should act, retry, wait, stop, ask for help, or escalate.
You evaluate behavior systematically. You use representative cases, traces, outcome checks, comparisons, and regression tests rather than treating a plausible response as proof of success.
You have shipped software that people or operational processes depend on and have worked through debugging, timeouts, inconsistent data, changing APIs, and production incidents.
You can investigate ambiguous problems independently, define a useful system boundary, explain trade-offs clearly, and turn decisions into working software.
You care about simplicity and control. You know when a deterministic workflow is better than an agent and when additional autonomy is justified by evidence.
You bring useful expertise and an independent perspective. Strong adjacent experience in workflow engines, developer tooling, distributed systems, automation platforms, or integration-heavy backend software can be highly relevant when paired with credible LLM-system understanding.

Around 2+ years of professional software-engineering experience is a useful guide, not a hard requirement. What matters is the technical depth of what you built, the decisions and production outcomes you owned, and your ability to learn unfamiliar systems.
You May Not Be a Great Fit If

Your LLM experience is mainly prompt engineering, chatbots, basic RAG, or connecting a model API to a user interface.
Your background is primarily offline data analysis, model training, or experimentation, and you do not want to own production software and operational behavior.
You treat retrieval as the complete agent architecture rather than one possible source of context within a larger execution system.
You consider a coherent model response successful without verifying the decision, tool call, state change, or real-world outcome.
You rely on an agent framework to provide the system design and are not comfortable reasoning about the control flow, state, permissions, and failure behavior underneath it.
You are not interested in owning evaluations, trace analysis, regression testing, and production learning alongside feature development.
You prefer fully scoped implementation tasks with stable requirements and limited responsibility for product or operational outcomes.

Benefits
Real ownership: you're not maintaining someone else's codebase, you're building a core, novel part of the product from the ground up.

Build at the core. Own a defining part of xHeron’s technology, from the first architectural decisions to production.
Shape the direction. Work directly with our CTO, challenge assumptions and help decide what we build, not just how.
Grow beyond the job description. We invest in your development, with room to expand your ownership and take on technical leadership as xHeron grows.
Share in the upside. Salary plus VSOP participation, so you can benefit from the value you help create.

Our Process

Intro call (15-30 min): a conversation with Friedrich (CTO) about your background, what you've built, and why this role.
Technical take-home case study: a short, real engineering problem, close to what you'd actually be building.
Case study interview (1 hour): you walk us through your thinking, not just the final code.
Culture fit (30 min): meet both Founders and make sure it's a fit both ways.

title: (Senior) Accountant/ Buchhalter*in (all genders) in Berlin
description_clean:
We're building the future of urban stays. One city at a time.
Homaris widmet sich einer der drängendsten Herausforderungen moderner Städte: Menschen aus aller Welt brauchen Orte, an denen sie leben, arbeiten und sich zuhause fühlen können. Wir entwickeln und betreiben vollständig digitalisierte Serviced Apartments in den großen Städten Deutschlands. Unser nächster Schritt: Europa und darüber hinaus.
Mit dem nanopartment® verfolgen wir eine Produktvision, die modernes Wohnen auf Zeit neu denkt – auf kleinstmöglichem Raum.
Unser Umsatz verdreifacht sich innerhalb von zwei Jahren – organisch und aus eigener Kraft. Ohne Venture Capital. Ohne Exit-Strategie. Wir denken langfristig und bauen unser Unternehmen konsequent danach auf.
Außergewöhnliche Menschen machen diese Entwicklung möglich. Jetzt suchen wir eine weitere Person, die diesen Weg mit uns gestaltet.
Your Role
Du arbeitest in unserem Finance-Team und verantwortest die korrekte und zuverlässige Buchung der Geschäftsvorfälle unserer Gesellschaften. Gemeinsam mit dem bestehenden Accounting-Team stellst du sicher, dass notwendige Zahlungen in allen Unternehmensbereichen korrekt abgewickelt und verbucht werden. Der Einsatz moderner Software-Lösungen beschleunigt und digitalisiert unsere Prozesse. Du nimmst eine zentrale Rolle im Unternehmen ein und stehst im regelmäßigen Austausch mit den verschiedenen Unternehmensbereichen.  
Diese Position richtet sich an eine Person, die eigenverantwortlich arbeitet, Prozesse aktiv mitgestaltet und gemeinsam mit Homaris langfristig wachsen möchte.
What You'll Do
Geschäftsvorfälle prüfen und buchen. Du stellst sicher, dass sämtliche Geschäftsvorfälle in DATEV korrekt erfasst werden.  
Debitoren- und Kreditorenbuchhaltung verantworten. Du erfasst die Vorgänge ordnungsgemäß und betreust außerdem die Anlagen- und Bankbuchhaltung.  
Zahlungseingänge und Zahlläufe steuern. Du kontrollierst die Zahlungseingänge und erstellst die erforderlichen Zahlläufe.  
Steuermeldungen übermitteln. Du übermittelst die Umsatzsteuervoranmeldungen und Übernachtungssteuererklärungen.  
Konten abstimmen. Du führst Abstimmarbeiten im Sachkonten-, Debitoren- und Kreditorenbereich sowie für Intercompany-Konten durch.  
Abschlüsse vorbereiten. Du übernimmst vorbereitende Tätigkeiten und arbeitest bei der Erstellung von Monats-, Quartals- und Jahresabschlüssen nach HGB mit.  
Kreditkartenabrechnungen bearbeiten. Du bearbeitest und buchst die Kreditkartenabrechnungen über Pleo.  
Prozesse digital weiterentwickeln. Du optimierst proaktiv Prozesse und erhöhst dabei den Digitalisierungsgrad.
What Makes You a Fit
Relevante Ausbildung und Erfahrung. Du hast eine abgeschlossene kaufmännische Ausbildung und mindestens drei Jahre Berufserfahrung in der Buchhaltung.  
Kenntnisse im deutschen Rechnungswesen. Du verfügst über Kenntnisse des HGB und des Umsatzsteuergesetzes.  
DATEV-Erfahrung. Du bringst Erfahrung mit der Buchhaltungssoftware DATEV mit.Weiterbildung als Pluspunkt. Idealerweise hast du eine Weiterbildung zum/zur geprüften Bilanzbuchhalter:in (IHK) abgeschlossen.  
Digitale Sicherheit. Du bist sicher im Umgang mit MS Office, insbesondere Excel, und offen für eine digitale Arbeitsumgebung.  
Eigenständigkeit und Teamgeist. Du arbeitest selbstständig und eigenverantwortlich, bist zugleich teamfähig und schaust gerne über den eigenen Aufgabenbereich hinaus.  
Verbesserungsorientierung. Du erkennst Verbesserungspotenziale und hast Interesse daran, deinen Bereich aktiv mitzugestalten und weiterzuentwickeln.  
Sprachkenntnisse. Du verfügst über sehr gute Deutschkenntnisse auf mindestens C1-Niveau sowie gute Englischkenntnisse auf mindestens B1-Niveau.  
KI-Affinität. Du nutzt digitale Tools mit Leichtigkeit, erkennst ihr Potenzial und bist begeistert davon, wie KI den Arbeitsalltag effizienter gestalten kann.  
Präsenz. Du arbeitest in Berlin oder bist bereit, nach Berlin zu kommen. Du arbeitest gerne persönlich mit anderen zusammen – denn genau so entsteht gute Arbeit.
The Environment
Homaris ist konsequent langfristig ausgerichtet. Wir investieren nicht in kurzfristiges Wachstum mit dem Ziel, schnell zu verkaufen. Wir bauen etwas Nachhaltiges und Substanzielles auf – und suchen Menschen, die diesen Weg gemeinsam mit uns gehen und langfristig Verantwortung übernehmen wollen.  
Das Tempo ist hoch. Die Herausforderungen sind anspruchsvoll und unmittelbar. Unser Team ist bewusst klein gehalten, sodass jede Person einen spürbaren Beitrag leistet.  
Wir nehmen uns nicht immer ausreichend Zeit, unsere Erfolge sichtbar zu machen und gemeinsam zu feiern. Daran arbeiten wir – und freuen uns, wenn du uns dabei unterstützt.
What We Offer
Wir definieren unsere Level nicht anhand von Jobtiteln oder Berufsjahren, sondern danach, welche Themen du eigenständig verantwortest und für welche Entscheidungen du einstehst.  
Darüber hinaus haben wir uns intensiv damit auseinandergesetzt, was Menschen brauchen, um ihre beste Arbeit zu leisten und gleichzeitig gut zu leben. Daraus ist ein Leistungspaket entstanden, das genau das widerspiegelt: Gesundheit, Mobilität, persönliche Entwicklung, Flexibilität und einige besondere Vorteile, die das Arbeiten in der Reise- und Hospitality-Branche mit sich bringt. Vieles ist bereits dabei.  
Die Details stellen wir dir gerne im persönlichen Gespräch vor.
Next Steps
Wenn dich diese Position anspricht, freuen wir uns darauf, mehr über deine Erfahrungen und deine Perspektive zu erfahren.

Wir nehmen uns Zeit, alle Bewerbungen sorgfältig zu prüfen, daher kann es 1-2 Wochen dauern, bis wir uns bei dir zurückmelden. Wir bitten dich um ein wenig Geduld und danken dir dafür!

title: Senior Product Manager (f/m/x)
description_clean:
Your Mission
This is a company built for growth, not comfort.  
When you join exmox, you're stepping onto a global, highly competitive playing field, solving real problems in environments that push you beyond your comfort zone.   
We build high-performing consumer products in one of the most competitive industries there is: mobile gaming, leading one of its largest innovations, a rewarded user engagement and acquisition platform that helps publishers acquire and retain players through rewarding experiences.  
Senior Product Manager (f/m/x) isn't just about shipping features, it's about building products that perform. Product at exmox means understanding the bigger business picture, considering cross-functional impact across Engineering, Data, Marketing, and Operations, and turning strategy into product decisions that create real value, knowing every change you ship affects millions of users. At exmox, we're also embracing AI as part of how we work, not just what we build. We use AI tools to work smarter, cut down on repetitive tasks and spend our time where it actually moves the needle. If that mindset speaks to you, you'll fit right in.  
If you're energized by dynamic markets, complex products, and the challenge of building products that perform at scale, we want to hear from you.  
What You’ll Own:

Own one of exmox's highest-impact product domains end-to-end, shaping the reward economy through payout thresholds, tiering, bonuses, promotions, and other key levers that drive profitability.
Drive activation, retention, and long-term engagement through onboarding experiences, streaks, quests, progression systems, reactivation flows, and other lifecycle initiatives.
Take new growth opportunities from first hypothesis to go/no-go decision, across product, market expansion, partnerships, and distribution.
Lead a high-quality experimentation process by defining hypotheses, designing statistically sound A/B tests, interpreting results, and making data-driven product decisions.
Partner closely with your dedicated Data Analyst to uncover opportunities, validate assumptions, and continuously improve product performance.
Work with Engineering, Design, Commercial, User Acquisition, Customer Support, Fraud, and Leadership to align priorities and deliver impactful product improvements.
Represent your product domain directly to leadership, using data, customer insights, and business context to influence strategic decisions.

What Success Looks Like:

You take ownership quickly: Within your first months, you've become the trusted owner of a critical product domain, confidently driving priorities, making decisions, and reducing dependency on leadership.
Growth metrics measurably improve: Your product strategy and experimentation drive meaningful improvements in activation, retention, and long-term user profitability.
Product decisions are driven by data: Experiments, user insights, and product analytics provide clear evidence to prioritize opportunities, validate ideas, and confidently decide what to scale - or stop.
Cross-functional teams are aligned around outcomes: You partner closely with Engineering, Design, Data, Commercial, and User Acquisition to deliver product improvements that balance user value with business impact.
You turn ambitious ideas into scalable growth: Through structured experimentation, clear prioritization, and continuous optimization, you build product experiences that become repeatable growth levers for the business.
You outgrow the role: We are hiring for the ceiling, not just the opening. This role is scoped to grow - mentoring other product managers first, and leading a product team as we scale, if that is the direction you want to take.

What You Bring

Experienced: You bring 5+ years of Product Management experience in consumer-facing digital products, ideally within mobile apps, gaming, marketplaces, subscriptions, ad-tech, fintech, or other high-growth B2C businesses. You have owned consumer product at scale - hundreds of thousands of monthly active users or more.
Business-Oriented: You understand that product decisions are business decisions. You're comfortable balancing user needs, commercial objectives, and technical constraints to maximize long-term value.
Fluent in Incentives: You have a real feel for why people come back and what makes a reward feel worth the effort. You have designed incentive, reward or progression mechanics and calibrated them so they motivate without eroding margin.
Experimentation-Driven: You have extensive experience running A/B tests, defining hypotheses, interpreting data, and making evidence-based product decisions. Statistical thinking comes naturally to you.
Data-Literate: You're comfortable working with product metrics and collaborating closely with analysts to uncover insights, measure success, and prioritize opportunities.
Strategic & Hands-on: You enjoy defining product strategy while remaining deeply involved in execution - from writing specifications and refining solutions to reviewing experiment results and driving delivery.
Collaborative: You build strong partnerships across Product, Engineering, Design, Analytics, Marketing, Commercial, and Leadership, bringing people together around clear product goals.
Intellectually Honest: You're comfortable working in ambiguity, take ownership without waiting for direction, and thrive in fast-moving environments where priorities evolve quickly. You also kill your own ideas when the data says so - being wrong early is cheaper than being right late.

How We Win

Speed is the feature. Speed beats rocket science. We move fast, test fast, and multiply our pace with AI, because action creates information and small wins compound. A fast failure is a lesson we learn from, a slow one is a problem we can't afford.
Focus on the essential. Done is better than perfect. We stay focused on what actually moves us forward and protect people's time from anything that doesn't. We're direct in how we communicate too, no rambling, no unnecessary detail.
See it. Own it. Solve it. The first to see it is best placed to fix it. We're not a place for comfort, we're a place for doers. "Not my job" isn't in our vocabulary, if you spot something, you help make sure it gets solved.
Respect others. Trust multiplies. Respect is non-negotiable. We disagree with ideas, never with people. Trust here is built the same way it is anywhere, through consistency, a thank you, a moment of listening, and owning your mistakes.
Perks that help you focus on what matters. Transport subsidy, learning budget, wellness and gym, workation, bi-weekly team lunches, and more. The perks are great, but the real reason people join and stay is the challenge, the ownership, and the drive to win together.

title: Senior Product Manager (f/m/x)
description_clean:
Your Mission
This is a company built for growth, not comfort.  
When you join exmox, you're stepping onto a global, highly competitive playing field, solving real problems in environments that push you beyond your comfort zone.   
We build high-performing consumer products in one of the most competitive industries there is: mobile gaming, leading one of its largest innovations, a rewarded user engagement and acquisition platform that helps publishers acquire and retain players through rewarding experiences.  
Senior Product Manager (f/m/x) isn't just about shipping features, it's about building products that perform. Product at exmox means understanding the bigger business picture, considering cross-functional impact across Engineering, Data, Marketing, and Operations, and turning strategy into product decisions that create real value, knowing every change you ship affects millions of users. At exmox, we're also embracing AI as part of how we work, not just what we build. We use AI tools to work smarter, cut down on repetitive tasks and spend our time where it actually moves the needle. If that mindset speaks to you, you'll fit right in.  
If you're energized by dynamic markets, complex products, and the challenge of building products that perform at scale, we want to hear from you.  
What You’ll Own:

Own one of exmox's highest-impact product domains end-to-end, shaping the reward economy through payout thresholds, tiering, bonuses, promotions, and other key levers that drive profitability.
Drive activation, retention, and long-term engagement through onboarding experiences, streaks, quests, progression systems, reactivation flows, and other lifecycle initiatives.
Take new growth opportunities from first hypothesis to go/no-go decision, across product, market expansion, partnerships, and distribution.
Lead a high-quality experimentation process by defining hypotheses, designing statistically sound A/B tests, interpreting results, and making data-driven product decisions.
Partner closely with your dedicated Data Analyst to uncover opportunities, validate assumptions, and continuously improve product performance.
Work with Engineering, Design, Commercial, User Acquisition, Customer Support, Fraud, and Leadership to align priorities and deliver impactful product improvements.
Represent your product domain directly to leadership, using data, customer insights, and business context to influence strategic decisions.

What Success Looks Like:

You take ownership quickly: Within your first months, you've become the trusted owner of a critical product domain, confidently driving priorities, making decisions, and reducing dependency on leadership.
Growth metrics measurably improve: Your product strategy and experimentation drive meaningful improvements in activation, retention, and long-term user profitability.
Product decisions are driven by data: Experiments, user insights, and product analytics provide clear evidence to prioritize opportunities, validate ideas, and confidently decide what to scale - or stop.
Cross-functional teams are aligned around outcomes: You partner closely with Engineering, Design, Data, Commercial, and User Acquisition to deliver product improvements that balance user value with business impact.
You turn ambitious ideas into scalable growth: Through structured experimentation, clear prioritization, and continuous optimization, you build product experiences that become repeatable growth levers for the business.
You outgrow the role: We are hiring for the ceiling, not just the opening. This role is scoped to grow - mentoring other product managers first, and leading a product team as we scale, if that is the direction you want to take.

What You Bring

Experienced: You bring 5+ years of Product Management experience in consumer-facing digital products, ideally within mobile apps, gaming, marketplaces, subscriptions, ad-tech, fintech, or other high-growth B2C businesses. You have owned consumer product at scale - hundreds of thousands of monthly active users or more.
Business-Oriented: You understand that product decisions are business decisions. You're comfortable balancing user needs, commercial objectives, and technical constraints to maximize long-term value.
Fluent in Incentives: You have a real feel for why people come back and what makes a reward feel worth the effort. You have designed incentive, reward or progression mechanics and calibrated them so they motivate without eroding margin.
Experimentation-Driven: You have extensive experience running A/B tests, defining hypotheses, interpreting data, and making evidence-based product decisions. Statistical thinking comes naturally to you.
Data-Literate: You're comfortable working with product metrics and collaborating closely with analysts to uncover insights, measure success, and prioritize opportunities.
Strategic & Hands-on: You enjoy defining product strategy while remaining deeply involved in execution - from writing specifications and refining solutions to reviewing experiment results and driving delivery.
Collaborative: You build strong partnerships across Product, Engineering, Design, Analytics, Marketing, Commercial, and Leadership, bringing people together around clear product goals.
Intellectually Honest: You're comfortable working in ambiguity, take ownership without waiting for direction, and thrive in fast-moving environments where priorities evolve quickly. You also kill your own ideas when the data says so - being wrong early is cheaper than being right late.

How We Win

Speed is the feature. Speed beats rocket science. We move fast, test fast, and multiply our pace with AI, because action creates information and small wins compound. A fast failure is a lesson we learn from, a slow one is a problem we can't afford.
Focus on the essential. Done is better than perfect. We stay focused on what actually moves us forward and protect people's time from anything that doesn't. We're direct in how we communicate too, no rambling, no unnecessary detail.
See it. Own it. Solve it. The first to see it is best placed to fix it. We're not a place for comfort, we're a place for doers. "Not my job" isn't in our vocabulary, if you spot something, you help make sure it gets solved.
Respect others. Trust multiplies. Respect is non-negotiable. We disagree with ideas, never with people. Trust here is built the same way it is anywhere, through consistency, a thank you, a moment of listening, and owning your mistakes.
Perks that help you focus on what matters. Transport subsidy, learning budget, wellness and gym, workation, bi-weekly team lunches, and more. The perks are great, but the real reason people join and stay is the challenge, the ownership, and the drive to win together.

You will establish when two structures represent the same chemical entity and when they do not, and handle stereoisomers, salts, tautomers, protonation and charge states and other representation and normalisation questions consistently.You will be the first person in this seat. You are comfortable making decisions on incomplete information, writing them down, and changing them when the data says so. title: Senior Frontend Engineer - React
description_clean:
ResearchGate is the professional network for scientists and researchers. From climate change and emerging diseases to food security and the responsible development of AI, the challenges facing our world are complex. Still, we’re optimistic about the power of millions of scientists working together to tackle them. We provide scientists with the help and support they need by connecting them to the world’s most active scientific community.
We've built a platform that gives the world's scientists the tools and services they need to connect, collaborate, and advance their research. Over 25 million members from 193 countries use ResearchGate to share, discover, and discuss research.
Objective of the role
We're looking for an enthusiastic frontend engineer with the skills and ability to turn great ideas into reality. You should have an in-depth understanding of current web technologies and front-end development, and be passionate about creating a great user experience. Your input will help us grow and maintain our React front-end.
Join a team that encourages you to explore, learn, and go beyond, while seeing your work lead to actionable results. Put your creative problem-solving and development skills into action and make a positive impact on science and society. This is a full-time position based in Germany.
The team 
You will be an integral part of the product team dedicated to enhancing ResearchGate's publisher-facing product. This role involves designing, constructing, and refining the platform to further our mission of facilitating global scientific connections and ensuring open access to research. At present, our team is working on making ResearchGate a great platform for publishers to connect with existing and future authors.
Your immediate colleagues will consist of JavaScript and PHP engineers, an Engineering Manager, a Product Manager, a UX Designer, and a UX Writer. Our team places great value on our collaborative and communicative work culture and we eagerly anticipate integrating a new Engineer into this environment.
Responsibilites 


Create web interfaces using TypeScript and React for new products and features.


Seamlessly integrate our front-end with our back-end world using GraphQL and PHP.


Maintain and improve existing features and related infrastructure.


Collaborate with Product Managers, Designers, and Software Engineers to deliver compelling publisher-facing products.


Requirements


5+ years frontend web development experience in TypeScript (React), CSS


Demonstrated ability to create code that is easily comprehensible, maintainable, and testable.


Eagerness to acquire new skills, delve into different technologies and programming languages, and a willingness to acknowledge areas where expertise may be lacking.


Approach problem-solving thoughtfully, embracing curiosity and maintaining an open-minded perspective.


You are comfortable incorporating AI-assisted development tools into your daily workflow and exercise strong engineering judgment when evaluating and refining their output.


Knowledge of GraphQL.


It would be a plus if you already had knowledge of relational and document-based databases (we use MongoDB and Postgres).


What we're looking for 


You take responsibility over your own solutions and continuously improve them.


You engage in proactive and efficient communication within our distributed work environment.


You focus on building a great product.


You excel at designing and creating coherent, user-centric interfaces that display complex information.



The interview process


We start with a short call with HR or an Engineering Manager to align on the details of the job inquiry.


There will be a longer discussion about your technical and professional experience and expectations with an Engineering Manager and another colleague.

Not just the schedule, but the order of work behind it. When two things compete, you decide, or you get the decision made and tell everyone affected. Open questions have an owner and a date. title: Architecte Cloud (F/H/NB)
description_clean:
SFEIR est un cabinet d'expertise technologique spécialisé dans la conception, l'architecture et l'industrialisation de solutions numériques sur-mesure. Nous accompagnons les organisations dans leurs transformations les plus complexes en combinant la rigueur du Software Craftsmanship avec la maîtrise des technologies d'avenir. Convaincus que la souveraineté numérique est un enjeu stratégique majeur, nous concevons des architectures sécurisées, performantes et indépendantes, portées par des partenariats solides avec des acteurs clés comme SENS et Scaleway. Acteur de référence sur l'intelligence artificielle, nous faisons évoluer les standards d'ingénierie modernes. À travers notre plateforme GenAI RAISE et notre statut de partenaire Anthropic Select (au sein du Claude Partner Network), nous plaçons le Context Engineering et l'IA générative au cœur de nos pratiques. 
Nos chiffres clés :

950 consultants passionnés par la tech et augmentés par l’IA
8 agences en France, au Luxembourg et en Belgique
Partenaire Anthropic Select au sein du Claude Partner Network
15 ans de partenariat avec Google Cloud, AWS, Microsoft, Databricks, Confluent...
+5000 personnes formées par an via le SFEIR Institute

Rejoindre SFEIR, c'est intégrer un collectif où la culture technique prévaut. Nous offrons des trajectoires de carrière dédiées aux experts (Individual Contributor / IC), te permettant de progresser en haute maîtrise technique sans devoir basculer vers du management organisationnel. Nous intégrons l'IA à nos propres pratiques d'ingénierie (utilisation quotidienne de RAISE et Claude Code) pour automatiser les tâches à faible valeur ajoutée et concentrer nos efforts sur la conception d'architectures résilientes.
▪️ À propos de la mission

Pour accompagner la forte croissance de notre collectif Sud-Ouest, nous recherchons notre futur Architecte Cloud confirmé (F/H/NB).
Tes missions au quotidien : 


Concevoir et déployer des architectures Cloud performantes et scalables (AWS, GCP, IaaS/PaaS/SaaS) adaptées aux besoins métiers et techniques
Piloter la migration d’applications et de workloads vers le Cloud, en choisissant les meilleures options (microservices, conteneurs Docker/Kubernetes, serverless, bases de données cloud)
Appliquer et promouvoir les bonnes pratiques DevOps et CI/CD (Jenkins, GitLab CI, Terraform, Ansible, ArgoCD) pour garantir performance, automatisation et fiabilité des déploiements
Assurer la sécurité et la conformité des environnements (IAM, KMS, VPC, chiffrement, audit, bonnes pratiques Cloud Security)
Collaborer avec les équipes DevOps, architectes et métiers pour garantir la cohérence technique et l’efficacité opérationnelle
Participer à la transformation Agile des projets Cloud et à l’amélioration continue des processus
Documenter les solutions et former les équipes clientes pour favoriser l’autonomie sur les environnements déployés


▪️ Le profil idéal


Expérience : Tu justifies d'au moins 5 ans d'expérience réussie en ingénierie et architecture Cloud (AWS ou GCP), avec une vraie pratique du terrain et du code d'infrastructure.


Expertise IaC & DevOps : Tu maîtrises l'automatisation via Terraform/Ansible, l'écosystème Kubernetes et les déploiements continus (ArgoCD/GitLab CI).


Culture d'Ingénierie : Tu possèdes une vision globale du SI (sécurité, réseau, stockage, FinOps) et tu aimes transmettre tes convictions techniques auprès des équipes de développement comme des décideurs.



▪️ L'ancrage Bordelais
L'agence SFEIR Bordeaux regroupe une quinzaine d'ingénieurs et d'architectes seniors. Tu y trouveras la proximité et l'agilité d'une structure à taille humaine, adossée à la solidité d'un grand groupe. Tu participes activement à l'écosystème tech local (meetups, conférences BDX/IO, SFEIR Talks) et tu peux intégrer le programme AI Champions pour piloter la R&D de l'agence.
▪️ Tes conditions de travail 


Organisation : 2 à 3 jours de télétravail par semaine.
Équipement : Laptop haut de gamme au choix (MacBook Pro ou Dell Precision dernière génération).
Package : Rémunération fixe attractive, prime de vacances, accord d'intéressement, forfait mobilités durables, mutuelle et titres-restaurant.


▪️ Le processus de recrutement 


Échange RH : Alignement sur ton parcours, tes attentes et les opportunités SFEIR.
Session Technique ("PlayOffs") : Évaluation pratique en pair-programming (Algo, AWS ou GCP avec du Terraform) avec deux Sfeirians. 
Échange Métier & Projection : Discussion approfondie sur les cas d'usage, les missions cibles et le contexte client à Bordeaux.
Entretien Final : Échange stratégique avec le Directeur d'Agence.

title: AI Engineer
Solutions Architect f/m/d
description_clean:
Apaleo is the world's most open, API-first property management platform powering the next generation of hospitality operations. Its modular, AI-powered infrastructure enables hoteliers to customise their tech stack, automate routine work, and deliver seamless, personalised guest experiences, powered by best-in-class apps and autonomous AI agents that adapt to every stay.
Why this role
You are the technical voice in front of strategic customers, at a moment when hospitality is being rebuilt around AI. We are launching our own AI agent platform, and we need architects who can show operators what comes next.

High trust. You own the technical answer in front of strategic customers and deals.
High visibility. Your work shows up in deals, key accounts and customer stories, and it reaches Product.
High freedom. You decide how to solve a problem, which tools to use and what to prototype.
Fast iteration. We test ideas within days, try new technology early and share what works.

Your mission
Win and grow strategic accounts with technical credibility, and turn what you learn in the field into input for the product. You look at a customer's current architecture and show how an Apaleo-centred setup delivers their goals. You also help them put AI agents to work, deciding what should be an agent, what it costs and how to set it up. Sales and Account Management own the relationship and the commercial terms. You own the technical answer.
What you will do

Technical discovery and solution scoping. Lead discovery where a standard demo is not enough. Write clear scopes covering what Apaleo delivers natively, what needs a short-term solution and what is out of scope.
Proofs of concept. Build fast, working proofs of concept (quick demos that show technical fit). Agree scope in writing first, and build in a safe test environment, never with live guest data.
Agents and automations. Design and build agents and automations for customer use cases, using n8n or Make today and Apaleo's own AI agent platform as it launches. Write code where agents need deterministic steps.
Hands-on delivery and short-term solutions. Work alongside the customer, building only where it unblocks a named deal, removes an adoption risk or fills a product gap. Agree an exit plan (an end date, a replacement and a named owner) before you start.
Post-sale health checks and expansions. Diagnose gaps against the go-live specification, run proactive checks (for example 90 days after go-live) and scope integrations for expanding customers.
Reusable assets. Turn every engagement into a reference architecture, pattern or template that the next twenty customers can use.
Thought leadership. Join prospect and customer conversations on how AI will change hospitality over the next two to three years.
Product feedback. Test new technology on real customer problems. Share prototypes and field evidence with Product, ending every experiment with a clear decision: adopt, hand over or drop.

How you work

You decide the approach, the stack and the order of work.
You protect three guardrails: written scope before a proof of concept, an exit plan before a custom build and no commercial promises.
You go from idea to prototype in days and show it early.
You think in systems and build for reuse, not one-off projects.
You share findings openly with Sales, Account Management and Product.

Who you work with
Sales/BD and Account Management (they call you in at defined deal triggers), Customer Success, Product, Security, Partnerships, RevOps and Senior Leadership. 
What you bring
Must have

Multiple years in solution architecture, solution engineering or technical consulting in B2B SaaS, ideally with complex software such as ERP or enterprise platforms
Strong API skills: REST, authentication, webhooks and events, and data-flow design
Hands-on workflow automation (n8n preferred) and practical experience building with LLM agents
A systems thinker with real AI curiosity, who uses AI tools day to day
Stakeholder management experience and credibility with executives and IT teams
Self-direction, an ownership mindset and the discipline to say no to scope that does not advance a deal
Curiosity that ends in working prototypes, not just opinions
Clear, structured documentation habits
Fluent English and French skills
Willingness to travel, including regularly to France and the UK

Strong plus

Hospitality or travel experience, including hotel operations and PMS concepts (reservations, folios, rate plans, night audit)
Experience with another cloud PMS, channel manager or payments integrations
Enterprise architecture experience on large, multi-site projects
Applied AI or ML background, or experience with MCP and agent platforms
SQL and BI fundamentals

How we measure success

Architecture engagements and blueprints delivered each quarter
Customer satisfaction with your contribution
Adoption of recommended apps, integrations and agents
Share of engagements served by an existing reusable pattern
Revenue impact e.g. deal unblocked, AI adoption, or churn averted

Your first 90 days

Days 1 to 30: Learn the platform and ways of working, shadow discovery and proof of concept work, and take over open customer projects.
Days 31 to 60: Lead technical discovery on live deals and run your first health check with Account Management.
Days 61 to 90: Deliver a proof of concept or short-term solution end to end with an exit plan, and share your first experiment with Product.

 
What We Offer
Culture & Growth

A Diverse & International Team: Work alongside passionate professionals from over 20 nationalities, bringing unique cultural perspectives, backgrounds, and experiences to shape the future of hospitality tech.
Growth & Development: As we scale, so do your opportunities. You'll benefit from 360° feedback reviews, a dedicated learning budget, and plenty of chances to take on more responsibility. Our evolving career framework ensures you have increasing opportunities to learn new skills, advance your career, and make an impact.
Autonomy & Ownership: Great ideas can come from anywhere. We empower you to take responsibility, make decisions, and contribute directly in an environment built on trust, transparency, and collaboration.
Shape the Future of Hospitality Tech: Be part of a fast-growing scale-up transforming the hospitality industry. From day one, your work drives real impact and you'll have the freedom to bring your ideas to life.
Competitive & Fair Compensation: We believe great work deserves great pay. Our salaries are competitive and guided by benchmarking data to ensure fairness across all roles and teams. We make sure to recognize and reward performance and contribution.

Perks & Lifestyle

Flexible & Remote Work Options: We focus on results, not clocking hours. You can work from home, the office or in a hybrid setup, with flexibility to adapt your schedule as long as it makes sense for your role, your team and our business.
Team Connection: Strong connections fuel collaboration. We celebrate and connect through regular team dinners, company meetups, Oktoberfest celebrations, Christmas parties, and other offsite events.
Paid Time Off: Enjoy 30 days of vacation to fully disconnect, recharge, and return inspired.
Health & Wellbeing: Prioritize your health with access to hundreds of gyms, fitness studios, and wellness options through our EGYM Wellpass membership.

title: Post-doctorant.e : "Simulation numérique 3D de l’infusion de composites à fibres naturelles" - CDD 12 mois
description_clean: ENGLISH VERSIONRejoindre Mines Saint-Étienne, c’est s’engager dans une institution où la science et l’innovation bâtissent un avenir plus durable. Une école d’excellence où chacun a l’opportunité de révéler son plein potentiel et de contribuer à relever les défis de demain.Classée parmi les meilleures écoles d’ingénieurs en France et reconnue mondialement, notre école, membre de l’Institut Mines-Télécom, forme les talents de demain tout en contribuant activement à relever les grands défis industriels, numériques et environnementaux. Avec nous, vous intégrez une communauté de 500 collaborateurs, 2500 étudiants, et participez à un projet ambitieux : conjuguer excellence académique, recherche d’avant-garde et impact sociétal positif.L’Institut Mines-Télécom fédère les grandes écoles françaises autour des défis industriels majeurs, numériques, énergétiques et écologiques. Avec ses 8 Grandes Écoles publiques et 2 écoles filiales, il est le premier institut public dédié aux ingénieurs et managers. Ensemble, nous imaginons et construisons un avenir durable, en formant les acteurs qui façonneront les transitions de demain.Bienvenue dans l’univers des matériaux du futur !Au centre Science des Matériaux et des Structures (SMS), rattaché au Laboratoire Georges Friedel (unité mixte de recherche CNRS), on décortique la matière pour mieux la maîtriser. Alliages métalliques, céramiques, composites… ici, on explore le lien entre procédés, microstructures et propriétés des matériaux.Grâce à des outils de caractérisation avancée et des modèles multi-échelles, nos enseignants-chercheurs inventent le concept de « Material by design » : concevoir les matériaux dès l’atelier de recherche, pour une performance sur-mesure.🧠 Vous aimez la science fondamentale qui change le réel ? C’est ici que ça se passe.🎯 Description du poste - ce que nous attendons de vousCe post-doctorat s’inscrit dans le cadre du projet ANR PRME LINEN (Experimental and Numerical Characterisation of Flax Composite Manufacturing by Liquid Infusion: From Local Phenomena to Induced Properties), auquel participent plusieurs chercheurs de l’École des Mines de Saint-Étienne, avec pour objectif d’étudier l’élaboration de pièces structurales en matériaux composites à base de fibres de lin.Ce post-doctorat, d’une durée de 12 mois est proposé pour développer la modélisation numérique de l’infusion de résine dans des préformes composites à fibres de lin. L’objectif est d’étudier, à l’échelle mésoscopique, l’influence de l’organisation anisotrope et hétérogène des torons de fibres sur l’écoulement de la résine. Le projet s’appuiera sur des simulations 3D par éléments finis, reposant sur un couplage Stokes-Darcy et la prise en compte d’un tenseur de perméabilité orthotrope. Une attention particulière sera portée à l’influence des variations locales de la fraction volumique de fibres sur la perméabilité, les chemins préférentiels d’écoulement et les effets capillaires. Les simulations seront réalisées avec le code éléments finis Cœur (https://gitlab.emse.fr/bruchon/Coeur), en s’appuyant sur la bibliothèque PETSc et des solveurs itératifs préconditionnés adaptés aux problèmes de grande taille. Dans un premier temps, des architectures idéalisées de type unidirectionnel, quasi-unidirectionnel et tissé seront étudiées à l’aide d’une représentation par Level-Set. Dans un second temps, lorsque cela sera possible, des mésostructures réalistes seront reconstruites à partir d’images µ-CT. Le post-doctorant.e contribuera également au développement et à la validation de la stratégie numérique et travaillera en interaction étroite avec les travaux expérimentaux et numériques des autres tâches du projet.   🔍 Ce que nous recherchonsUne formation en mécanique numérique, mécanique des fluides, éléments finis ou calcul scientifique est recherchée. Des compétences en C++/Python, calcul haute performance, PETSc, méthodes Level-Set ou traitement d’images 3D seront appréciées.Vous vous reconnaissez dans les capacités et aptitudes suivantes :· Capacité à travailler en équipe· Capacité à dialoguer avec des interlocuteurs académiques et industriels 📩 Candidatez dès maintenant !Date limite de candidature :  20/11/2026🔗 Les dossiers de candidature (CV, lettre de motivation, lettre de recommandation) sont à déposer sur la plateforme RECRUITEE : https://institutminestelecom.recruitee.com/o/post-doctorante-simulation-numerique-3d-de-linfusion-de-composites-a-fibres-naturelles-cdd-12-moisPrise de poste envisagée : 1er février 2027Les candidats retenus après examen de leur dossier de candidature seront auditionnés en entretien par visioconférence puis, le cas échéant, reçus pour un entretien en présentiel à Mines Saint-Étienne.Dans le cadre de sa politique Égalité, Diversité et Inclusion, l’École des Mines de Saint Etienne est un employeur soucieux de l’équité de traitement entre les candidatures. ℹ️ Informations complémentairesCDD de droit public d’une durée de 12 moisLa rémunération sera fixée selon le profil du candidat, en fonction des règles définies par le cadre de gestion de l’Institut Mines TélécomTemps plein - profil CadrePoste basé à Saint-Étienne à l’École des Mines. title: Senior Quantum Fault-Tolerance Architect (f/m/d)
description_clean: eleQtron develops and operates full-stack quantum computers based on trapped-ion technology. Our approach combines laser schemes for cooling/initialization/readout, engineered magnetic-field gradient induced coupling (MAGIC) combined with microwave control for universal gate sets, and advanced quantum control techniques and dedicated firmware to work within the high-fidelity regime and below the error threshold of quantum error correction (QEC).A central objective of our technology roadmap is the realization of fault-tolerant quantum computing. To achieve this goal, we combine the above high-fidelity quantum hardware with microscopic physics-based modelling, hardware–software co-design, advanced characterization and benchmarking techniques, and detailed numerical simulations to model system performance realistically and identify the optimal QEC strategy and the associated system requirements.As part of our initiative towards fault-tolerant quantum computing, we are expanding our Foundations & Concepts team and are looking for a Senior Quantum Fault-Tolerance Architect (f/m/d) to help establish and grow this strategic activity within the company.Role Overview:As Senior Quantum Fault-Tolerance Architect (f/m/d), you will help shaping eleQtron’s long-term roadmap towards logical quantum computing, driving research activities in quantum error correction and fault tolerance, contributing to key architectural decisions, coordinating cross-functional efforts across hardware, software, system architecture and applications, and playing a leading role in building and growing the company’s fault-tolerance capability. Responsibilities: Develop and drive fault-tolerant quantum-computing strategies and logical architectures for trapped-ion MAGIC quantum processors.Lead hardware-aware quantum error-correction studies and guide architectural decisions for future processor generations.Coordinate realistic performance models connecting hardware characterization, circuit-level noise models, and logical performance metrics.Work closely with System Architecture, System Operations, Software Engineering, and Quantum Applications teams to support the co-design of future fault-tolerant quantum computers.Contribute to the development and mentoring of a growing fault-tolerance team while supporting eleQtron’s long-term technology roadmap. title: Analytical Chemistry Specialist - Freelance AI Trainer Project
description_clean:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, which manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for an Analytical Chemistry Specialist – Freelance AI Trainer Project based in Germany.
Are you an analytical chemistry expert interested in contributing to the next generation of artificial intelligence? This freelance opportunity allows you to apply your scientific expertise to train and evaluate advanced AI models designed to support scientific discovery, education, and laboratory research. You will assess AI-generated responses to complex analytical chemistry questions, identify inaccuracies, and strengthen scientific reasoning across a wide range of applications. Your work will help improve the accuracy, reliability, and practical relevance of AI-generated scientific knowledge. Working remotely and independently, you will contribute specialized insights to the development of more capable and trustworthy AI systems. This role is ideal for experienced chemistry professionals who enjoy solving complex problems, communicating scientific concepts, and exploring the intersection of chemistry and emerging technology.
Accountabilities

Evaluate AI-generated scientific content: Review responses to theoretical and practical analytical chemistry questions, assessing their factual accuracy, logical consistency, scientific rigor, and relevance to real-world laboratory applications.
Apply specialized analytical chemistry knowledge: Develop and evaluate scenarios involving spectroscopy, chromatography, electrochemical analysis, quantitative chemical analysis, environmental testing, pharmaceutical analysis, and analytical method development.
Assess advanced analytical techniques: Challenge AI models on mass spectrometry, high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC), gas chromatography (GC), nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) interpretation, trace analysis, titrimetric methods, and related instrumentation.
Identify and document model weaknesses: Record reproducible errors, reasoning gaps, inaccurate interpretations, and other failure patterns to support systematic improvements in model performance.
Contribute to AI training and evaluation: Provide detailed scientific feedback, propose corrections, and recommend improvements to prompts, evaluation criteria, and testing methodologies.
Support scientific quality assurance: Apply principles of method validation, quality assurance and quality control (QA/QC), and analytical data interpretation to evaluate the reliability of AI-generated outputs.
Communicate scientific reasoning clearly: Explain conclusions, demonstrate analytical approaches, and document the steps behind technical judgments to help improve model transparency and reliability.

Requirements

Education: A PhD in analytical chemistry or a closely related chemical science discipline is preferred. Equivalent advanced expertise supported by relevant professional or research experience may also be valuable.
Technical expertise: Strong knowledge of analytical chemistry principles, instrumentation, spectroscopy, chromatography, electrochemical methods, quantitative analysis, and analytical method development.
Research or laboratory experience: Experience in laboratory-based research, analytical method validation, pharmaceutical or environmental testing, instrumentation-intensive studies, or related scientific applications is highly desirable.
Specialized analytical skills: Familiarity with techniques such as mass spectrometry, HPLC, GC, NMR, trace analysis, titrimetry, and laboratory QA/QC procedures.
Scientific evaluation skills: Ability to identify factual inaccuracies, assess scientific arguments, interpret experimental scenarios, and distinguish sound conclusions from flawed reasoning.
Written communication: Excellent technical writing skills and the ability to explain complex scientific concepts clearly, precisely, and logically.
Analytical thinking: Strong critical-thinking, problem-solving, and attention-to-detail skills, with the ability to break down complex problems and document reproducible findings.
AI training readiness: Interest in evaluating AI-generated content, identifying model limitations, and contributing to the development of more reliable scientific AI systems.
Working arrangements: Ability to work independently in a remote freelance environment, manage assignments effectively, and provide a secure computer and reliable high-speed internet connection.

Benefits

Competitive hourly compensation: A pay range of $8–$65 per hour, with the final rate determined by expertise, professional experience, and geographic location. The final offer may vary from the advertised range.
Remote flexibility: Work remotely from India, with the flexibility associated with a freelance contract arrangement.
Meaningful scientific impact: Help shape AI systems that may support scientific education, research, analytical problem-solving, and laboratory workflows.
Intellectually stimulating work: Apply advanced analytical chemistry knowledge to challenging scientific questions and emerging AI evaluation tasks.
Specialized professional contribution: Use your research, instrumentation, and laboratory expertise in an innovative technology-focused environment.
Independent contractor arrangement: Manage your work in a freelance capacity, subject to project requirements and applicable engagement terms.
Benefits clarification: This is a contract position. Company-sponsored benefits, including health insurance and paid time off (PTO), are not provided. Contractors are responsible for supplying their own computer and high-speed internet connection.

title: Co-Founder & CTO @ AI Model Efficiency Engine Venture, Berlin
description_clean: This is an Atlantic portfolio venture.About the VentureAI models have moved faster than most companies’ ability to put them to work. The capabilities are there; knowing how to combine them effectively is still catching up.Frontier labs naturally put their own models first. Companies often follow suit, asking one general-purpose model to handle ten very different jobs. We believe there is far more to unlock in the models that already exist, even before the next generation arrives. That is the opportunity we are building around.We bring closed providers and open-weight models together behind a single API. With no proprietary model to promote, we can choose the right combination for the task. Our engine breaks requests into their component parts, routes each to the right model within a cost budget, fine-tunes on customer data and checks the result against agreed quality standards. Think ten specialists working on ten pieces, rather than one generalist carrying the whole task.Lower costs matter because of what they make possible: giving a small team the freedom to build something that would previously have required a much larger one.Our founder was selected for Slush 20 Under 20, awarded by Anthropic, Slush, Index Ventures and Sifted, and brings considerable drive, a hands-on approach and a strong sense of urgency to building the company. We closed our pre-seed round in two weeks. With people already waiting to use the product, we are looking for a technical co-founder to help shape what comes next and bring it into production.About the RoleAs co-founder and CTO, you will help shape the company as well as its technology. Working alongside the founder as an eye-level partner, you will turn the ambition into an architecture, a product and an engineering team capable of delivering it.aYour remit spans the efficiency engine, the platform beneath it and the people building both. You will lead our founding AI engineer and backend platform engineer, grow the team and establish the standards that guide its work. You have led engineering before, but stayed close to the code, and want to keep building as your responsibilities grow.Two things define the technical challenge here. Efficiency is the product itself, so routing, fine-tuning, caching, quantization and open-weight serving sit at the heart of the roadmap. Agentic engineering is also central to how we work. You will set the standard for using individual agents and entire agent fleets effectively, building the harnesses and workflows that allow a small team to move quickly while retaining sound engineering judgement.There is a lot to build and an ambitious timeline ahead. We work with relentless intensity, move quickly from decisions to execution and look for people who take initiative and see things through. You will have the scope to make consequential decisions early, and the responsibility to turn them into something that works.What you’ll doYou will move between architecture, code and company building, setting the technical direction while building the team that delivers it.Lead the engineering team: guide our founding AI engineer and backend platform engineer, review their work and establish the engineering and operational standards, including on-call and incident response.Build the team: lead technical hiring and decide how engineering grows as the company develops.Set the technical direction: make the architectural calls, shape the roadmap and decide what we build ourselves and where we use existing tools and services.Develop the efficiency engine: bring together routing, semantic and prefix caching, parameter-efficient fine-tuning, distillation, quantization and batching, with inference economics informing each decision.Own open-weight serving: choose and operate vLLM, SGLang or equivalent, including GPU capacity and European hosting, alongside closed providers through a single interface.Make quality measurable: build rigorous eval harnesses and the evidence needed to establish whether a cheaper route still meets the agreed standard.Build the platform underneath it: own the gateway API, provider layer, identity and tenancy, precise usage and cost accounting, secure storage of customer keys and European infrastructure as code, with GDPR and data residency requirements built in.Stay hands-on: write code and play an active part in designing and building the platform and cost-efficiency systems. Develop our agentic engineering setup, from harness design and benchmarking to the agent workflows that help the team ship.Represent the company technically: bring depth and clarity to customer pilots, enterprise security reviews and investor conversations.About YouYou have grown into engineering leadership without losing the instinct to build. When faced with a difficult problem, you explore what would make it possible and look for a workable path through it, weighing failure modes alongside unit economics. AI has changed how you work, and you have taken the time to understand where it helps, where it fails and how to use it well.We are looking for depth in five areas:Engineering leadership: you have been a CTO, VP Engineering, Head of Engineering or engineering lead, ideally in a startup. You have hired and led engineers, established standards and taken responsibility for both the architecture and what the team shipped.Backend and platform engineering: you bring deep experience in distributed systems, API design, streaming, Postgres, Kubernetes, Terraform and cloud operations, with a broad understanding of what makes a platform reliable and scalable. You have taken systems into production, operated them under significant load and worked through incidents yourself.LLM cost efficiency: you have reduced costs in a production system and can explain the numbers, the decisions behind them and the trade-offs involved. Your experience covers techniques such as LoRA or QLoRA, routing, caching, quantization, distillation and batching, grounded in an understanding of serving economics.Open-weight models in production: you have served, tuned, evaluated and operated open models under load, including the GPU and capacity decisions that come with them.Agentic engineering: you build on strong coding fundamentals, with practical experience running agent fleets and designing and benchmarking their harnesses. You can reason independently about the code they produce and take responsibility for its quality.You also bring a disciplined approach to LLM benchmarking: thoughtful eval design, statistical honesty and a willingness to reproduce results before relying on them.Fluent English is required; German is a plus.Nice to haveA strong open-source record, particularly in AI infrastructure or inference, with real users.Experience with LiteLLM, NVIDIA NIM, TGI, llama.cpp or similar, and with self-hosted or air-gapped enterprise deployments.Experience with European cloud providers such as Scaleway, Hetzner or OVH.Experience working in startups tackling similar technical challenges.Why JoinWith the pre-seed round closed and the first steps already taken, you will join at a point where there is momentum to build on and considerable room to shape what comes next. You will build alongside the founder, choose and grow the engineering team, and receive co-founder equity in the business you help create.The architecture, efficiency engine, security model and engineering culture are all still yours to shape. The decisions you make now will become the foundations for everything that follows.We are entering a market where competitors have larger teams, more funding and an earlier start. Our conviction is that technical depth, focused decisions and a small team that works well together give us a meaningful opportunity to compete. Identify root causes of material or coating deviations and execute real-time operational problem-solving. • Lab Equipment Ownership: Manage, calibrate, and maintain key equipment (different types of mixers, coating/calendering lines, diagnostic tools), manage routine calibration and preventative maintenance, and draft practical SOPs.• EHS Rigor: Maintain a clean, organised, and safe laboratory environment, strictly following chemical handling and safety protocols.
